headline: High-risk default conflict: nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets while ComfyUI is offline-only, creating data leakage and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI has no filesystem read/write or MCP, so it cannot directly ingest nullclaw output by default. But nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use stdin/stdout, browser, and MCP, so if ComfyUI outputs are copied into its workspace or web channels, prompt-like content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are manually copied into nullclaw workspace files or web channels
IF nullclaw is configured to treat imported text as instructions
mitigations: Disable any workflow that imports ComfyUI text into nullclaw prompts
Keep ComfyUI outputs in a separate directory
Use read-only handoff files
Add a manual review step before nullclaw acts on imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while ComfyUI can operate on local model files and workflows. Because nullclaw has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, any shared workspace or copied artifacts can leak sensitive data outward. ComfyUI is offline-only, but the pair still exposes secrets through nullclaw's default surfaces.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are placed in nullclaw's workspace
IF nullclaw is given access to files containing secrets or tokens
mitigations: Store secrets outside any shared workspace
Restrict nullclaw to a dedicated non-secret directory
Rotate any tokens that were ever present in the workspace
Disable broad egress for runs that touch imported files
Review audit logs after any shared-file transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write files or modify git state, so it is not a write competitor. nullclaw can write files, modify git, and spawn subprocesses, creating conflict if both are pointed at the same workspace or repo. The overlap is real but one-sided, so the blast radius is limited to clobbering shared artifacts rather than symmetric contention.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same workspace or git repository
IF nullclaw performs writes while ComfyUI is generating artifacts in that location
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent
Make ComfyUI output directories read-only to nullclaw
Pause nullclaw before any git operation on shared repos
Use file locks for shared artifact directories

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows and artifacts that nullclaw may ingest through files, stdin/stdout, browser, or webhooks. nullclaw has action-taking surfaces and broad tool use, so if it treats ComfyUI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. There is no built-in verification shown in either profile, so the interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF nullclaw consumes ComfyUI-generated text or metadata without verification
IF nullclaw triggers actions based on generated workflows or captions
mitigations: Require human approval before nullclaw acts on ComfyUI output
Add schema validation for exchanged artifacts
Log provenance on every transferred file
Block direct execution of generated instructions

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-only and mainly handles media/model assets, while nullclaw handles conversation history, memory, audit logs, and secrets with broad egress. That creates a compliance mismatch on retention and sensitive-data handling if the same data class is routed through both. The profiles do not show a specific residency regime, so I cite the documented retention/secrets asymmetry instead of assuming one.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive data is routed through nullclaw
IF retention or deletion expectations differ between ComfyUI artifacts and nullclaw logs
mitigations: Separate regulated data from general workflows
Set a short retention policy for nullclaw logs
Avoid storing secrets in shared artifacts
Document which data classes may cross the boundary
